newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson's mansion goes on auction block.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson's mansion goes on auction block.

text.p: O.J. Simpson's mansion goes on the auction block on Monday at a minimum price of $2.5 million, but the money is unlikely to go toward satisfying a $33.5 million judgment against him because a local bank recently foreclosed on the house.
A civil court jury awarded the judgment to Simpson's children and the family of Ronald Goldman for the deaths of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Goldman.

But a local bank, Hawthorne Savings and Loan, recently foreclosed on Simpson's dream house at 360 North Rockingham Avenue in the exclusive Brentwood neighbourhood when he failed to make mortgage payments for several months.
The bank has first claim to the proceeds of the auction, followed by Simpson's lawyers, who are still owed a considerable amount from Simpson's trials.
His lawyer Ronald Slates told CNN the house would have to realise at least $4.3 million to pay off the bank and the lawyers before any proceeds would go toward the damages settlement.
Real estate agents, however, said the house was unlikely to fetch much more than the asking bid.
The former football star was found not guilty of the 1994 murders of his ex-wife and Goldman by a criminal court jury in 1995, but was held liable for their deaths by a civil jury this year.

The 6,000-square-foot (560-sq.-metre) house, which Simpson bought in 1977, has five bedrooms, six bathrooms, a tennis court, a waterfall, an Olympic-sized swimming pool and a guest house once occupied by Kato Kaelin, who became America's most famous lodger during Simpson's first trial.
The contents of the home were not part of Monday's sale. They will be auctioned off later this year to help pay some of the damages awarded by the civil jury.

In order to bid at the auction, being held on the steps of the Los Angeles County courthouse in suburban Norwalk, prospective buyers had to bring $2.5 million in cash or a certified check for that amount. If no one wants the property or is unwilling to make the minimum bid, the bank will be the owner of the corner lot mansion.
According to court documents, the property has been appraised at between $4 million and $6 million, but the publicity and notoriety surrounding it could alter that price.
The mansion is just two miles (3.2 km) from Nicole Brown Simpson's condominium, where she and Goldman were stabbed and slashed to death in an attack on the night of June 12, 1994.

Simpson has continued to maintain his innocence, even after being found liable for the deaths. "No. Did not do it. Don't feel I could ever hurt anybody. I think I've spent my life being a good guy," he told CNN's Greta Van Susteren in an interview, part of which was aired on Monday.

His mansion was first seen by a nation of television viewers a few days after the murders as the white Ford Bronco driven by his friend Al Cowlings, with Simpson inside, pulled into the driveway accompanied by a phalanx of police cars following the notorious slow-speed chase that ensued after he failed to surrender to be charged with the murders.
It was also the place where a bloody glove was found the day after the murders, along with drops of blood.
Simpson's criminal defence team maintained the glove, which matched one at the murder site, was planted by Los Angeles police Det. Mark Fuhrman, who they painted as a racist, rogue cop.

Many Brentwood residents said they saw the sale of the Rockingham estate as the final act in a saga that has brought unwelcome attention to the neat, tree-lined area from both the media and tourists gawking at the now-famous grounds.
